intel.t: lower costs, end the Iran war and tariff taxes, and get money out of politics.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: a Washington insider in the pocket of lobbyists who took the same money he now attacks, plus the partner lobbying ad and the 68 tax increases claim, which PolitiFact rated False.
Democrats coalesced quickly, 75 percent satisfied with him as nominee per TIME; volunteers had contacted close to half a million voters by October 21.
national Democrats Newsom, Harris, Warnock and Buttigieg came in for him in October; Sununu called the Newsom visit irrelevant to New Hampshire.
outside spending favors Sununu $36.1M to $19.3M in the general election, through October 23.

bottom: Pappas has far outraised John E. Sununu but is being outspent on the air by outside groups. VoteLog, reading FEC data, shows Pappas at $23,703,648 raised, $22,126,867 spent and $1,984,366 in cash through October 14, 2026, against Sununu's $5,681,528 raised, https://votelog.org/investigations/new-hampshire-senate-general-money. Outside groups had spent $36,057,061 benefiting Sununu and $19,279,169 benefiting Pappas in the general election. Pappas says outside groups are outspending him 3 to 1 on TV, per the New Hampshire Bulletin, https://newhampshirebulletin.com/2026/09/03/pappas-is-making-campaign-finance-part-of-his-us-senate-bid-his-opponents-cry-hypocrisy/.
Interests with money and a decision:

**Small donors.** More than 165,000 unique donors and about 95 percent of gifts at $100 or less, per his campaign, https://chrispappas.org/2026/10/chris-pappas-for-senate-announces-q3-fundraising-haul-of-more-than-8-1-million/.
**Party and leadership.** WinSenate, the Senate Majority PAC vehicle, spent $15,036,083 for him, the largest single outside spender in the race.

intel.t: a focused, New Hampshire first, town to town campaign that avoids partisanship and stresses who he is as a leader.

intel.l: Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it
intel.t: fifteen years cashing in as a Washington lobbyist for corporate interests, and being a rubber stamp for Trump after endorsing the One Big Beautiful Bill.
Republicans, 85 percent satisfied with him, and independents who give him a 10 point edge on character, per TIME.
outside groups and the RNC reportedly field about 1,000 paid canvassers for him, including AFP, America PAC, Sentinel Action and Turning Point.
NHPR cancelled its Senate forum after Sununu declined citing his schedule, leaving one more debate.

bottom: Sununu's own campaign is small. Outside money is carrying him. VoteLog shows his campaign at $5,681,528 raised, $3,936,991 spent and $1,711,396 in cash through October 14, 2026, with no self funding, https://votelog.org/investigations/new-hampshire-senate-general-money. Outside groups had spent $36,057,061 benefiting him in the general election, against $19,279,169 for Pappas.
Three interests combine money and a decision:

**Billionaire megadonors.** The Senate Leadership Fund, funded by Elon Musk at $168 million cycle wide, Miriam Adelson at $30 million and others, spent $11,118,531 for him. Americans for Prosperity Action, America PAC and Protect Freedom PAC add Koch, Musk and Jeff Yass money.
**Trump world.** No Going Back PAC, backed by MAGA Inc.'s $200 million cycle wide, spent $14,037,292 for him. Trump endorsed him on February 1, 2026.

D.t: Chris Pappas leads by 10.8 in the forecast and wins 95% of simulations. The cushion is about 74,157 votes; a one point swing is about 3,446 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +2.5 and D +19.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +7.2. Your best recent poll is InsiderAdvantage (R) at D +9.9; your worst is New York Times/Siena University at D +4.3. 9 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Hillsborough, a projected net 19,636 votes; Strafford, a projected net 14,064 votes; Grafton, a projected net 13,949 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Hillsborough, D +10.1, 28.3% of the vote; Rockingham, D +3.6, 24.4% of the vote; Belknap, R +8.5, 4.9% of the vote; Carroll, D +4.9, 4.3% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Chris Pappas runs furthest behind in Belknap, Rockingham. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 94% of voters, 52 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.69 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 73% of voters, 54 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.67 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 59% of voters, 58 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.96 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Chris Pappas: Immigration voters 26 to 70, Voters who can afford daily costs 47 to 49, Men 47 to 49. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$4.3M cash against $2.5M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Activity: 3 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.
